findings.title: Keep functions short — under ~50 lines
findings.message: The processOrder function now spans 67 lines (lines 8–74), exceeding the ~50-line guideline. Extract sub-helpers for validation, discount calculation, tax calculation, shipping calculation, persistence, notification, and inventory updates into separate named functions to keep the main function concise and focused.

claims.claim: The processOrder function spans 67 lines (lines 8–74).
claims.reason: The diff shows the function body starting at line 5 (the function declaration) and the last line of code is at line 74 (the return statement). Counting from line 8 (first line after the function declaration) to line 74 gives 67 lines of function body. This is directly visible in the diff.

claims.claim: Extracting sub-helpers will keep the main processOrder function concise and focused.
claims.reason: The rule document's 'Good' example demonstrates that extracting sub-helpers results in a concise, focused main function that is easier to understand. The rule document states 'Functions that span many screens are hard to keep in working memory and usually do more than one thing. Extract sub-helpers.' This directly supports the claim that extraction improves focus and conciseness.

findings.title: Keep cyclomatic complexity low
findings.message: The processOrder function has high cyclomatic complexity due to nested conditionals (coupon type check, premium tier check, region-based tax calculation, shipping conditions, loyalty tier logic) combined with multiple sequential operations. Refactor by extracting discount calculation, tax calculation, and shipping calculation into separate named functions with early returns to reduce complexity below 10.

claims.claim: The processOrder function has high cyclomatic complexity.
claims.reason: The diff shows the processOrder function contains multiple nested conditionals (coupon type check with if/else if, premium tier check, region-based tax calculation with multiple if/else if branches, shipping conditions with if/else if/else) and sequential operations (validation, discount calculation, tax calculation, shipping calculation, persistence, notifications, analytics, loyalty, inventory, audit logging). The rule document states that functions with deeply nested conditionals and many independent branches are hard to test and reason about, and the code exhibits this pattern. However, the actual cyclomatic complexity metric is not explicitly calculated in the evidence provided.

claims.reason: The diff clearly shows nested conditionals for coupon type checking at lines 23-28: 'if (order.coupon) { if (order.coupon.type === 'percent') { ... } else if (order.coupon.type === 'fixed') { ... } }'

claims.claim: The processOrder function has a premium tier check.
claims.reason: The diff shows a premium tier check at lines 29-31: 'if (order.user.tier === 'premium') { discount += subtotal * 0.05; }'

claims.reason: The diff shows region-based tax calculation at lines 34-39 with multiple conditional branches: 'if (region === 'CA') tax = subtotal * 0.0725; else if (region === 'NY') tax = subtotal * 0.08875; else if (region === 'TX') tax = subtotal * 0.0625; else tax = subtotal * 0.05;'

claims.claim: The processOrder function has shipping conditions.
